summary:
**Conversation Overview**

Bethany, who runs The Luxora Collective (TLC), requested help building a standardized SOP template to be used consistently across all company procedures. Claude created a branded Word document template with a fixed nine-section structure: title block and metadata table (covering SOP number, owner, version, review dates, and approver), followed by Purpose, Scope, Roles and Responsibilities, Definitions and Systems Required, Procedure (phase-based with verb-led numbered steps), Quality Standards and Definition of Done, Common Pitfalls, Related Documents, and Revision History. Every section includes italic guidance text and bracketed placeholders so authors know exactly what to fill in.

Following delivery of the template, Claude flagged two structural gaps: the absence of a defined SOP numbering convention and the lack of a master register to prevent duplicate numbers or ungoverned drift. Bethany confirmed she wanted both addressed. Claude then produced two additional documents. The SOP Standards sheet (Word) serves as the library's front matter, defining the numbering format (TLC-SOP-[FUNCTION]-[###]), six function codes (SAL for Sales, DEL for Client Delivery, MKT for Marketing, REC for Recruiting, OPS for Operations, FIN for Finance), document and brand voice rules (no em dashes, no contractions, verb-led steps), ownership and approval workflow, six-month review cadence with versioning rules, storage requirements, and the four-state lifecycle (Draft, In Review, Active, Retired). The Master SOP Index (Excel) is a living register with dropdown validation on Function and Status columns, conditional formatting that highlights overdue review dates in red and dates due within 30 days in amber, status color coding, and a Reference tab restating all codes and definitions. Claude seeded four real SOPs from the existing library as starter rows, noting that assigned owners and effective dates are placeholders for Bethany to confirm.

Claude noted two remaining gaps at close: the approval structure currently allows self-review since Bethany owns and approves most SOPs, and the index only captures existing procedures rather than planned ones. Claude offered to assign default approvers per function once Bethany confirms the split, and to add a "Planned" status with seeded rows for obvious missing procedures (closer hiring, setter hiring, client kickoff, monthly check-in). A colleague named Aanchal was noted as the likely owner of the Setter Playbook SOP. All three deliverables share the same brand palette (charcoal, warm taupe gold, soft cream) and formatting style established in the template.

     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `extract-text`, or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	> **Script paths:** every `scripts/...` command in this document is relative to **this skill's directory** (the directory containing this `SKILL.md`). Run them from here, or prefix with the skill's absolute path.
    22	
    23	### Converting .doc to .docx
    24	
    25	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Reading Content
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	# Text extraction as markdown
    35	extract-text document.docx
    36	
    37	# Show tracked changes instead of accepting them
    38	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    39	
    40	# Raw XML access
    41	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    42	```
    43	
    44	### Converting to Images
    45	
    46	```bash
    47	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    48	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    49	ls page-*.jpg
    50	```
    51	
    52	`pdftoppm` zero-pads the page number to the width of the total page count (so a 12-page PDF produces `page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`, not `page-1.jpg`). Use the `ls` to get the actual filenames before reading them.
    53	
    54	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    55	
    56	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    57	
    58	```bash
    59	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    60	```
    61	
    62	---
    63	
    64	## Creating New Documents
    65	
    66	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    67	
    68	### Setup
    69	```javascript
    70	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    71	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    72	        InternalHyperlink, Bookmark, FootnoteReferenceRun, PositionalTab,
    73	        PositionalTabAlignment, PositionalTabRelativeTo, PositionalTabLeader,
    74	        TabStopType, TabStopPosition, Column, SectionType,
    75	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,

    77	
    78	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    79	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    80	```
    81	
    82	### Validation
    83	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    84	```bash
    85	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    86	```
    87	
    88	### Page Size
    89	
    90	```javascript
    91	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    92	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    93	sections: [{
    94	  properties: {
    95	    page: {
    96	      size: {
    97	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    98	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    99	      },
   100	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
   101	    }
   102	  },
   103	  children: [/* content */]
   104	}]
   105	```
   106	
   107	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
   108	
   109	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
   110	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   111	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   112	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   113	
   114	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   115	```javascript
   116	size: {
   117	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   118	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   119	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   120	},
   121	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   122	```
   123	
   124	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   125	
   126	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   127	
   128	```javascript
   129	const doc = new Document({
   130	  styles: {
   131	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   132	    paragraphStyles: [
   133	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   134	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   135	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },

   141	  },
   142	  sections: [{
   143	    children: [
   144	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   145	    ]
   146	  }]
   147	});
   148	```

   152	```javascript
   153	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   154	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   155	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   156	
   157	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET

   159	  numbering: {

   161	      { reference: "bullets",
   162	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,

   165	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   166	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },

   171	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   172	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   173	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   174	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   175	    ]
   176	  }]

   179	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   180	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)

   186	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.

   406	## Editing Existing Documents
   407	
   408	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   409	
   410	### Step 1: Unpack
   411	```bash
   412	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   413	```
   414	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   415	
   416	### Step 2: Edit XML
   417	
   418	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   419	
   420	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   421	
   422	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   423	
   424	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   425	```xml
   426	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   427	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   428	```
   429	| Entity | Character |
   430	|--------|-----------|
   431	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   432	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   433	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   434	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   435	
   436	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   437	```bash
   438	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   439	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   440	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   441	```
   442	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   443	
   444	### Step 3: Pack
   445	```bash
   446	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   447	```
   448	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   449	
   450	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   451	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   452	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   453	
   454	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   455	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   456	
   457	### Common Pitfalls
   458	
   459	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   460	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   461	
   462	---
   463	
   464	## XML Reference
   465	
   466	### Schema Compliance
   467	
   468	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   469	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   470	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   471	
   472	### Tracked Changes
   473	
   474	**Insertion:**
   475	```xml
   476	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   477	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   478	</w:ins>
   479	```
   480	
   481	**Deletion:**
   482	```xml
   483	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   484	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   485	</w:del>
   486	```
   487	
   488	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   489	
   490	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   491	```xml
   492	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   493	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   494	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   495	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   496	</w:del>
   497	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   498	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   499	</w:ins>
   500	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   501	```
   502	
   503	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   504	```xml
   505	<w:p>
   506	  <w:pPr>
   507	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   508	    <w:rPr>
   509	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   510	    </w:rPr>
   511	  </w:pPr>
   512	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   513	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   514	  </w:del>
   515	</w:p>
   516	```
   517	Without the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.
   518	
   519	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   520	```xml
   521	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   522	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   523	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   524	  </w:del>
   525	</w:ins>
   526	```
   527	
   528	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   529	```xml
   530	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   531	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   532	</w:del>

   539

   542	**CRITICAL: `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` are siblings of `<w:r>`, never inside `<w:r>`.**
   543	
   544	```xml
   545	<!-- Comment markers are direct children of w:p, never inside w:r -->
   546	<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/>

from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side
from openpyxl.worksheet.datavalidation import DataValidation
from openpyxl.formatting.rule import FormulaRule, CellIsRule
from datetime import date

INK="FF26242B"; DARK="FF2B2730"; ACCENT="FFA6885F"; ACCENT_DK="FF8A6F4C"
CREAM="FFF4EEE6"; GREY="FF6E6A73"; RULE="FFD8CFC2"; WHITE="FFFFFFFF"

wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "SOP Index"

thin = Side(style="thin", color="FFD8CFC2")
border = Border(left=thin, right=thin, top=thin, bottom=thin)

# Title
ws.merge_cells("A1:K1")
ws["A1"] = "THE LUXORA COLLECTIVE  |  MASTER SOP INDEX"
ws["A1"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=15, bold=True, color=DARK)
ws["A1"].alignment = Alignment(horizontal="left", vertical="center")
ws.row_dimensions[1].height = 30

ws.merge_cells("A2:K2")
ws["A2"] = "Single register of every standard operating procedure. Numbers are assigned here and never reused. Review each SOP at least every six months."
ws["A2"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, italic=True, color=GREY)
ws.row_dimensions[2].height = 18

headers = ["SOP Number","SOP Title","Function","Process Owner","Approver",
           "Version","Status","Effective Date","Last Reviewed","Next Review Due","Location / Link"]
hrow = 4
for i, h in enumerate(headers, start=1):
    c = ws.cell(row=hrow, column=i, value=h)
    c.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, bold=True, color=WHITE)
    c.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=DARK)
    c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="left", vertical="center", wrap_text=True)
    c.border = border
ws.row_dimensions[hrow].height = 26

# Seed rows (real SOP names from the library; owners and dates are starters to confirm)
seed = [
    ["TLC-SOP-SAL-001","Sales Closer SOP","SAL","Bethany","Bethany","1.0","Active", date(2026,1,15), date(2026,1,15), date(2026,7,15),""],
    ["TLC-SOP-SAL-002","Generic Sales Training SOP (role agnostic)","SAL","Bethany","Bethany","1.0","Active", date(2026,1,20), date(2026,1,20), date(2026,7,20),""],
    ["TLC-SOP-SAL-003","Setter Playbook (six outreach channels)","SAL","Aanchal","Bethany","1.0","Active", date(2026,2,1), date(2026,2,1), date(2026,8,1),""],
    ["TLC-SOP-DEL-001","Sales Call Analysis and Conversion Audit (Upwork SOP)","DEL","Bethany","Bethany","1.0","Active", date(2026,2,10), date(2026,2,10), date(2026,8,10),""],
]
r = hrow + 1
for row in seed:
    for i, val in enumerate(row, start=1):
        c = ws.cell(row=r, column=i, value=val)
        c.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color=INK)
        c.border = border
        c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="left", vertical="center")
        if i in (8,9,10):
            c.number_format = "mmm d, yyyy"
        if i in (3,6):
            c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")
    r += 1

# Blank styled rows for future entries
for _ in range(16):
    for i in range(1, 12):
        c = ws.cell(row=r, column=i)
        c.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color=INK)
        c.border = border
        c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="left", vertical="center")
        if i in (8,9,10):
            c.number_format = "mmm d, yyyy"
        if i in (3,6):
            c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal="center", vertical="center")
    r += 1
last = r - 1

widths = [18,42,10,15,14,9,11,14,14,15,24]
for i, w in enumerate(widths, start=1):
    ws.column_dimensions[ws.cell(row=1, column=i).column_letter].width = w

ws.freeze_panes = "A5"

# Data validation: Function (C) and Status (G)
dv_func = DataValidation(type="list", formula1='"SAL,DEL,MKT,REC,OPS,FIN"', allow_blank=True)
dv_stat = DataValidation(type="list", formula1='"Draft,In Review,Active,Retired"', allow_blank=True)
ws.add_data_validation(dv_func); ws.add_data_validation(dv_stat)
dv_func.add(f"C5:C{last}")
dv_stat.add(f"G5:G{last}")

# Conditional formatting: Next Review Due overdue / due soon
red_fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFF4D7D7"); red_font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color="FFB42318", bold=True)
amber_fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="FFFBEFD6"); amber_font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color="FF9A6A00")
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"J5:J{last}",
    FormulaRule(formula=[f'AND($J5<>"",$J5<TODAY())'], fill=red_fill, font=red_font))
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"J5:J{last}",
    FormulaRule(formula=[f'AND($J5<>"",$J5>=TODAY(),$J5<=TODAY()+30)'], fill=amber_fill, font=amber_font))

# Conditional formatting: Status colors
green_font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color="FF2E7D32", bold=True)
grey_font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color=GREY, italic=True)
amber_font2 = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color="FF9A6A00", bold=True)
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"G5:G{last}", CellIsRule(operator="equal", formula=['"Active"'], font=green_font))
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"G5:G{last}", CellIsRule(operator="equal", formula=['"In Review"'], font=amber_font2))
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"G5:G{last}", CellIsRule(operator="equal", formula=['"Draft"'], font=grey_font))
ws.conditional_formatting.add(f"G5:G{last}", CellIsRule(operator="equal", formula=['"Retired"'], font=Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color=GREY, strike=True)))

# ---------- Reference sheet ----------
rs = wb.create_sheet("Reference")
rs.merge_cells("A1:B1")
rs["A1"] = "SOP NAMING AND STATUS REFERENCE"
rs["A1"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=13, bold=True, color=DARK)
rs.row_dimensions[1].height = 26

rs["A3"] = "Number format"
rs["A3"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=11, bold=True, color=ACCENT_DK)
rs["A4"] = "TLC-SOP-[FUNCTION]-[###]"
rs["A4"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=12, bold=True, color=INK)
rs["A5"] = "Three digit number runs in sequence within each function, starting 001. Numbers are never reused."
rs["A5"].font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, italic=True, color=GREY)

def block(start, title, rows, w1=14, w2=70):
    rs.cell(row=start, column=1, value=title).font = Font(name="Calibri", size=11, bold=True, color=ACCENT_DK)
    hr = start + 1
    for j, htext in enumerate(["Code" if "Function" in title else "Status","Meaning"], start=1):
        cc = rs.cell(row=hr, column=j, value=htext)
        cc.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, bold=True, color=WHITE)
        cc.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=DARK); cc.border = border
    rr = hr + 1
    for code, meaning in rows:
        a = rs.cell(row=rr, column=1, value=code); a.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, bold=True, color=INK)
        a.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor=CREAM); a.border = border
        b = rs.cell(row=rr, column=2, value=meaning); b.font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, color=GREY)
        b.border = border; b.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical="center")
        rr += 1
    return rr

nxt = block(7, "Function codes", [
    ("SAL","Sales: setting, closing, pipeline, and sales call analysis"),
    ("DEL","Client Delivery: Revenue Leak Audit, Market Blueprint, and Growth Engine execution"),
    ("MKT","Marketing: ads, content, outreach, and partner campaigns"),
    ("REC","Recruiting and Hiring: sourcing, hiring briefs, and onboarding"),
    ("OPS","Operations: internal systems, coordination, and administration"),
    ("FIN","Finance: billing, reporting, and financial planning"),
])
nxt = block(nxt + 1, "Status definitions", [
    ("Draft","Being written. Not yet approved and not in use."),
    ("In Review","Complete and awaiting approval from the function lead or CEO."),
    ("Active","Approved and in force. This is the version the team follows."),
    ("Retired","Replaced or no longer used. Kept for record. Its number is not reused."),
])
rs.cell(row=nxt+1, column=1, value="Review cadence").font = Font(name="Calibri", size=11, bold=True, color=ACCENT_DK)
rs.cell(row=nxt+2, column=1, value="Review every SOP at least every six months. Overdue review dates show red in the index; dates within 30 days show amber.").font = Font(name="Calibri", size=10, italic=True, color=GREY)
rs.merge_cells(start_row=nxt+2, start_column=1, end_row=nxt+2, end_column=2)
rs.column_dimensions["A"].width = 14
rs.column_dimensions["B"].width = 78

wb.save("/home/claude/TLC_SOP_Index.xlsx")
print("saved")

Two pieces, matched to the template so the three form one set.

The SOP Standards sheet is the front matter for the library. It defines the numbering convention (TLC-SOP-[FUNCTION]-[###]), the six function codes (SAL, DEL, MKT, REC, OPS, FIN), document and brand voice rules, ownership and approval, the six-month review cadence with versioning rules, where SOPs live, and the four-state lifecycle (Draft, In Review, Active, Retired).

The Master SOP Index is a working register, not a static table. It has dropdowns on Function and Status, conditional formatting that turns a review date red when overdue and amber when due within 30 days, and status color coding (Active green, Retired struck through). A Reference tab restates the codes, status definitions, and cadence inside the file. I seeded four real SOPs from your library as starter rows.

One thing to confirm rather than assume: the seeded owners and dates are placeholders. I assigned the Sales Closer SOP, generic training SOP, and Sales Call Analysis SOP to you, and the Setter Playbook to Aanchal, with effective dates as guesses. Correct those and they become real records.

Two weakest parts and the stronger version:

The function codes baked in the approval rule as "function lead, or CEO where the lead is the owner," but TLC has not formally named a lead per function. Right now you own most of the seeded SOPs and also approve them, which means there is no second set of eyes. The stronger version names a default approver per function in the standards sheet, for example Eric approves FIN and OPS, you approve SAL and DEL and MKT, so approval is never self-review. Tell me the split and I will write it in.

The index covers SOPs that already exist but does not capture what is missing. The higher-leverage version adds a short "planned" section or a flag so the index doubles as a build queue, showing which procedures the business still needs but has not written. Given you are scaling closers, setters, and a marketing partner, the gaps are where the risk is. I can add a Status value of "Planned" and seed the obvious missing ones (closer hiring, setter hiring, client kickoff, monthly check-in) so the index shows the whole map, not just what is done.
